site.name: Velorki
site.tagline: Plan the ride, find the café, follow the turns, and do all of it where the signal ends. Free, open source, built on OpenStreetMap.
site.description: Velorki plans bike routes, builds loops and records your rides — on the phone, offline, on OpenStreetMap data. Free and open source.

appearance.hint: The app ships light and dark with five accents. Switching here swaps every screenshot on this page.

alt.loop: A generated loop: a round trip drawn on the map with its length, climbing and surface mix.
alt.search: Offline place search: a list of nearby cafés and drinking water taps with their distance, found without a connection.
alt.navigation: Turn-by-turn navigation: the next turn in a banner above the map while the route is being followed.

meta.title: Velorki — bike route planner and ride recorder, offline and open source
meta.description: Plan bike routes, generate loops, search places and follow spoken turns — all on the phone, with no connection. Free, open source, built on OpenStreetMap.

hero.title: Ride where the signal ends
hero.lead: Plan the ride, find the café, follow the turns, and do all of it where the signal ends. Free, open source, built on OpenStreetMap.
hero.body: Download a region once and the whole app works without a network: the map, the routing, the place search and the spoken turns. No account, no ads, no paywall on the ride itself, and no server in the loop unless you ask for one.
hero.storesPending: The store listings are not live yet. The source and the builds are on GitHub in the meantime.

free.title: Everything on the phone is free
free.body: Planning, loops, offline maps and routing, search, navigation, recording, ride stats, GPX and FIT files — for everyone, for good. The routing data and the search index are mirrored for you at no charge.

features.title: What it does
features.lead: Six things you will use on every ride. Every screenshot below is the real app.

plan.title: A route for the bike you are on
plan.body: Tap waypoints on the map and the route is calculated on the phone, on downloaded 5°×5° tiles. Touring, road, gravel, MTB and direct profiles, up to three alternatives, the elevation profile and a breakdown of the surfaces you will ride on.

bullets.one: Five bike profiles, up to three alternatives per route
bullets.two: Elevation profile and surface statistics for every option
bullets.three: An online routing server is optional, for areas with no tiles

loops.title: “A 60 km round trip from here via the lake”
loops.body: Say how far you want to ride and, if you like, one place to pass. Candidates are generated on the phone and scored on length, climbing, surface and repeated roads, so what comes back is a ride, not a detour.

bullets.one: Round trips that come back to where you started
bullets.two: Scored on length, climbing, surface and repeated roads
bullets.three: Pick a place to pass and the loop goes through it

offline.title: The map, the routing and the search, with no connection
offline.body: Each routing tile brings a search index of its places, streets with house numbers and points of interest: cafés, drinking water, toilets, repair stations, shelters, bike shops, campsites, hotels, passes, peaks, viewpoints, stations and landmarks. Typing “water” lists the nearest taps by distance, and typos are corrected from the index itself.

bullets.one: Vector map areas saved per region
bullets.two: Search by category: cafés, water, toilets, repair stations
bullets.three: Online place search is one tap away

navigate.title: Spoken turns, on the phone
navigate.body: A turn banner and spoken cues while you ride a route, re-routing on the phone when you leave it, compass or north-up follow modes. The cues are generated from the same routing data that planned the ride, so they work where there is no network.

bullets.one: Turn banner and voice cues, offline
bullets.two: Re-routes on the device when you leave the line

record.title: It keeps recording when the phone does not
record.body: Recording runs in the background with a foreground notification on Android and a live activity on iOS, and survives the app being killed. Battery saver dims the screen and coarsens the GPS. Afterwards, ride pages with elevation, speed, splits and a speed-coloured track.

bullets.one: Background recording that survives the app being killed
bullets.two: Auto-pause, battery saver, distance, time, speed and ascent
bullets.three: Ride pages with splits and a speed-coloured track

files.title: Your rides are files you own
files.body: GPX and FIT import and export through the share sheet and open-with, so routes and rides move to Komoot, Garmin Connect, Strava or anything else that reads those formats. Strava and Ride with GPS connections and share links are the Plus part.

bullets.one: GPX and FIT in and out, from Files, Mail or a browser
bullets.two: A library of saved routes and recorded rides
bullets.three: Strava, Ride with GPS and share links with Plus

comparison.title: Free is everything that runs on the phone
comparison.lead: Velorki Plus is a small subscription only for the parts that need our servers or a partner account. Everything else is free, for everyone, for good.

rows.planning: Route planning, five bike profiles, alternatives
rows.files: GPX and FIT import and export
rows.assistant: The assistant: a sentence becomes a route
rows.rwgps: Ride with GPS: routes and trips both ways
rows.sharing: Share links for routes and rides

comparison.note: The code for all of it is here, so you can also run your own relay and skip the subscription entirely.

openSource.title: Open source, open data
openSource.body: Velorki is open source under the AGPL: the app, the relay and this website. Everything it draws, routes on and searches in comes from OpenStreetMap, the map anyone can edit. So anyone can read the code, check what it does and improve it.

account.a: No. There is no account and no sign-up, not even for Velorki Plus — a subscription is restored through the store you bought it in, without an account with us.

offline.q: Does it really work without a connection?
offline.a: Yes. Download a region once and the map, the routing, the place search and the spoken turns all run on the phone. Only the assistant, the Strava and Ride with GPS connections and share links need a network, and those are the Plus features.

price.a: Everything that runs on the phone is free: planning, loops, offline maps and routing, search, navigation, recording, ride stats and GPX and FIT files. Velorki Plus is a subscription for the server-side features; the current price is shown in the app, in your currency, by the store.

plus.a: A small subscription for the parts that need our servers or a partner account: the assistant, the Strava connection, the Ride with GPS connection and share links. It is bought, managed and cancelled in the App Store or Google Play.

data.a: Nothing, unless you ask for it. Routes, rides and settings are stored on the device. The assistant asks for consent before any text leaves, and rounds the position it sends to about a kilometre. Map tiles and online search are fetched only when you are not using downloaded data.

osm.q: Where does the map data come from?
osm.a: From OpenStreetMap, under the ODbL. The map, the routing and the place search all run on that open data; the projects and licences behind it are on the credits page.

opensource.a: Yes. The app, its pure-Dart packages, the relay and this website are AGPL-3.0-only; all of it is on GitHub. The name, logo and icon are reserved, so a fork has to rebrand before publishing it to a store.

selfhost.q: Can I run the server parts myself?
selfhost.a: Yes. The relay, a routing server and a tile host can all be self-hosted; the repository has the compose files and the systemd units. A fork that points at its own relay needs no subscription at all.

cta.title: Get the app and ride
cta.body: Free on both stores, and the source is on GitHub. No account, no ads, no trial on the parts that run on your phone.

meta.title: Velorki Plus
meta.description: Velorki Plus is a small subscription for the parts that need our servers or a partner account: the assistant, Strava, Ride with GPS and share links.

plus.title: Velorki Plus
plus.lead: Everything that runs on your phone is free. Plus pays for the parts that need our servers or a partner account.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.body: Describe the ride you want in a sentence — “40 km, mostly gravel, a café stop” — and Velorki turns it into a route and plans it on your phone. The model runs behind a relay that holds the key; the app never sees it.

strava.title: Strava connection
strava.body: Upload a recorded ride to Strava and import your Strava routes into the library.

rwgps.title: Ride with GPS connection
rwgps.body: Routes and trips both ways, between Ride with GPS and your library.

sharing.title: Share links
sharing.body: Turn a route or a ride into a link anyone can open in a browser, with the map, the stats and a GPX download.

plus.freeBody: Planning, loops, offline maps and routing, search, turn-by-turn navigation, recording, ride stats and GPX and FIT files stay free, with or without Plus.
plus.priceBody: See the price in the app. The store shows the current monthly and yearly price in your own currency, with a free trial, and the price is never quoted here so it cannot go stale.
plus.restoreBody: Already subscribed? Restore purchases in Settings → Velorki Plus. Restoring works without an account: the store you bought it in is the only record.
plus.cancelBody: The subscription renews automatically at the end of each period unless it is cancelled at least 24 hours before. Payment is taken by the App Store or Google Play, where the subscription can be managed or cancelled at any time. A free trial that is not cancelled becomes a paid subscription.
plus.selfHostBody: The relay is open source. Point a build at your own and every Plus feature works without a subscription.

download.title: Get Velorki
download.lead: Free on both platforms. Everything that runs on the phone works without an account and without a connection.
download.storage: About 60 MB for the app, plus whatever you download in map and routing regions.
download.apkBody: Every release is tagged on GitHub with its APK attached, for people who would rather not use a store. Updates are manual when you install this way.
download.sourceBody: The whole app is in the repository. `mise install` in the root installs Flutter, Java and Node at the pinned versions; the app README has the rest.

credits.title: Credits
credits.lead: Velorki is built on open data and open source. These are the projects behind the map, the routes, the search and the type, with the licences they are published under.

osm.title: OpenStreetMap
osm.body: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. The map data Velorki draws, routes on and searches in comes from OpenStreetMap.
osm.licence: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0; rendered tiles under CC BY-SA 2.0.

brouter.title: BRouter
brouter.body: The routing engine. Velorki plans bike routes with BRouter and ships its routing profiles; the routing that runs on the phone follows the same upstream source. © Arndt Brenschede and contributors.

openfreemap.title: OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles
openfreemap.body: Vector map tiles by OpenFreeMap, built with OpenMapTiles from OpenStreetMap data. OpenFreeMap serves the default map style and requires no key.
openfreemap.licence: Software under the MIT licence, the OpenMapTiles schema and styles under BSD 3-Clause, the tiles under ODbL 1.0, the design attributed as © OpenMapTiles.

cyclosm.title: CyclOSM
cyclosm.body: The optional cycling overlay: a cycle-oriented map style for OpenStreetMap, served by the OpenStreetMap Foundation's tile servers.

photon.title: Photon
photon.body: Online place search, by komoot. Photon geocodes the place names typed into the search field and the names the assistant proposes, and is built on OpenStreetMap data. © komoot GmbH and contributors.

fonts.title: Barlow Condensed and Manrope
fonts.body: The two typefaces of the app and this website. Copyright 2017 The Barlow Project Authors, copyright 2018 The Manrope Project Authors.

maplibre.title: MapLibre GL
maplibre.body: The map renderer: MapLibre GL in the app and MapLibre GL JS on the share pages of this website.

flutter.title: Flutter
flutter.body: The framework the app is built with, together with the Dart packages that come with it.

credits.appNote: The full list of third-party licences, including every Dart package in the app, is in the app itself, under Settings → About → Open-source licences.
